description:
We are a STEM-focused team interested in space exploration, planetary science, and engineering. Our goal is to develop an innovative project that identifies Earth locations similar to the Moon and Mars, helping improve future space exploration and habitat research.

We welcome motivated members interested in coding, AI, data analysis, geology, physics, hardware, 3D design, and scientific research. We value creativity, teamwork, curiosity, and problem-solving.
summary:
ASTRO VADE must provide a fully functional scientific exploration platform with accurate, interactive maps of Earth, the Moon, and Mars. It must connect to genuine NASA and other trusted scientific datasets using valid, tested APIs and mapping services.

All planetary maps must use appropriate coordinate systems, projections, and geographic data. Users should be able to zoom, pan, rotate, switch layers, and explore real satellite imagery, elevation models, topographic maps, and geological features.

The platform must display scientifically accurate information about craters, volcanoes, faults, tectonic structures, and other geological features. Every dataset must include its source, observation date, spatial resolution, coordinates, and measurement units.

All diagrams and visualisations must be generated from genuine scientific measurements whenever available. Simulated illustrations must be clearly identified and never presented as real observations.

The development team must diagnose and fix NASA connection failures, broken maps, invalid endpoints, CORS issues, and rendering errors. Earth, Moon, and Mars must be tested independently.

ASTRO VADE must preserve its existing design, remain responsive, and never fabricate data or claim successful connections without verification.
details:
ASTRO VADE is an interactive scientific exploration platform designed to make space and planetary research more accessible. It allows users to explore Earth, the Moon, and Mars through interactive maps, scientific imagery, geological information, and research tools. The platform aims to connect real scientific datasets from NASA and other trusted organizations, helping users understand planetary environments and compare their geological characteristics.

Its main benefits are making scientific information easier to access, supporting students and researchers, and encouraging interest in astronomy, planetary science, and space exploration. Its intended impact is to democratize scientific exploration by providing free access to reliable information and helping users investigate potential locations for future exploration missions.

The project uses web development technologies, programming languages, interactive mapping systems, 3D visualization, and scientific APIs. Its development focuses on integrating real datasets rather than relying on fictional illustrations or unverified information.

ASTRO VADE is creative because it combines planetary exploration, scientific research, interactive visualization, and AI-assisted learning in one platform. Important factors considered include scientific accuracy, data reliability, accessibility, affordability, user experience, performance, and future scalability.
